purpose: Bounded method evidence, not recipe findings or publication authorization.

sources.publisher: Cattlemen’s Beef Board / National Cattlemen’s Beef Association
sources.access: Relevant full page text read through web open.
sources.claim: For less-tender large beef cuts, use low heat, liquid and a tight lid; dry surfaces aid even browning. Deglazing recovers browned pan deposits. Fork tenderness determines the texture finish; opening the lid loses heat/moisture and can extend cooking.
sources.application: Beef pot roast/brisket methods. Check liquid and lid dependencies and texture endpoint.
sources.exclusion: Not a validated pork formula or timing rule; no requirement to add a sear to every culturally distinct braise, and no universal liquid depth.

sources.access: Relevant full page text read through web open.
sources.claim: Whole beef/pork roasts: 145°F (63°C), then 3-minute rest. Ground meat: 160°F (71°C). Leftovers: 165°F (74°C).
sources.application: Match food category and measure internal temperature.
sources.exclusion: Minimum safety temperatures do not establish tenderness, cooking duration, cooling/storage limits or every preparation-specific hazard.

editorialChecksNotSourceClaims: Identify animal, cut, bone, dimensions, cooking vessel, covered/uncovered stages, liquid losses and target slice/shred texture.
Account for marinating, preheat, browning batches, slow cooking, resting and reduction without treating parallel steps as sequential.
unknowns: Pork-specific tenderness timing and collagen kinetics not established here. Confirm through appropriate source or testing; do not transfer beef times mechanically.
limits: No recipe-specific blind-reference findings used. No kitchen test. Quantities, yields, safety changes and identity changes require exception review.
